newsitem.title: USA: U.S. aid to Haiti hurts, not helps, group says.
newsitem.headline: U.S. aid to Haiti hurts, not helps, group says.

text.p: A private aid group said on Wednesday U.S. food aid to Haiti was destroying the impoverished island nation's ability to feed itself.
Grassroots International said that a flood of food aid was overwhelming local farmers who could not compete.
"They actually ignore the Haitian food producers," said Tim Wise, executive director of the Massachusetts-based aid organisation. "They are implementing a flawed policy."

At a news conference, Grassroots released preliminary findings of a six-month study of the impact of U.S. food aid to Haiti, mainly wheat, rice and vegetable oil, which cost U.S. taxpayers nearly $200 million over the past three years.
A spokeswoman for USAID said the agency, which oversees U.S. aid programmes for Haiti, disagreed strongly with the report.
"Food aid has made more food available to the Haitian people at a lower price and has increased food security in Haiti, significantly benefiting the poor," the spokeswoman said.
"Grassroots International seem to be against the principle associated with free market economies," she said.
Grassroots said the flood of food aid had driven down cereal prices and many peasant farmers had given up trying to compete. Local rice producers had gone out of business.

It said U.S. and international lending agencies had conditioned their assistance on Haiti agreeing to slash tariffs on imported goods, a policy which has also discouraged farmers since they cannot match the lower prices of imports.
The United States is the biggest of the international donors to Haiti, which distribute about 100 million tonnes of food aid there each year.
